en.name: Anthony the Great
en.summary: Egyptian hermit whose retreat into the desert made him the founding father of Christian monasticism.
en.body: Anthony was born to a prosperous Egyptian family around 251 and, after hearing the Gospel call to sell all he had and follow Christ, gave away his inheritance and withdrew into the desert to live as a hermit. Over decades of solitude, fasting, and spiritual combat with temptation, he attracted disciples who settled near him, and the loose communities that formed around his example became the template for later organized monasticism. Athanasius of Alexandria's biography of him, the Life of Antony, spread his fame across the Christian world and shaped how the Church would think about ascetic life for centuries. He died around 356, reportedly at the age of 105.
